question: What is the main purpose of a health referral system?

options.A: To generate more revenue for large tertiary hospitals
options.B: To prevent patients from ever visiting traditional healers
options.C: To reduce the number of staff needed at rural health posts
options.D: To move patients smoothly between different levels of care

explanation: A referral system connects basic clinics with advanced hospitals to ensure continuous and appropriate patient care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why is a functional referral network important for big teaching hospitals?

options.A: It eliminates the need for community health nurses altogether
options.B: It guarantees that every patient gets admitted for surgery
options.C: It prevents minor health issues from clogging up specialist care
options.D: It ensures that doctors only work half-day shifts

explanation: When primary clinics handle minor cases and only refer severe ones, tertiary hospitals can focus on complex medical conditions. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h1)

question: Which government tier is primarily responsible for managing Primary Health Care centers?
explanation: Primary health care services in Nigeria are closest to the grassroots and are managed by the local government authorities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: A patient with a complex heart condition requiring open-heart surgery should be sent to which level of care?
explanation: Tertiary facilities like teaching hospitals have the advanced equipment and specialists required for complex surgeries. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h2)

question: What does two-way communication mean in a referral system?

options.A: The ambulance driver talks directly with the hospital gatekeeper
options.B: The family calls the clinic every morning and evening
options.C: Information goes to the hospital and feedback returns to the clinic
options.D: The patient speaks to both the doctor and the nurse at the same time

explanation: Two-way communication ensures the referring nurse learns what happened to the patient and how to manage them during follow-up. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: A pregnant woman with obstructed labor is kept at a primary health clinic for three days trying local herbs before referral. Which principle of referral was violated?
explanation: Delayed transfer in an emergency violates the principle of timeliness, putting the mother and baby at severe risk. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h3)

question: Which symptom in a newborn or young infant is a clear indication for urgent hospital referral?

options.A: Mild sneezing during the early morning hours
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the skin on day four
options.C: Inability to breastfeed or drink anything
options.D: Sleeping for six hours straight at night

explanation: An infant who cannot feed is showing a dangerous sign of severe illness that requires immediate hospital evaluation. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: A pregnant woman at a primary health clinic presents with facial swelling, blurred vision, and a blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Give her paracetamol tablets and ask her to wait
options.B: Advise her to drink plenty of palm wine and sleep
options.C: Send her home with instructions to rest for a week
options.D: Refer her urgently to a secondary or tertiary facility

explanation: These are signs of severe pre-eclampsia, which can quickly lead to deadly eclamptic seizures if not managed in a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h4)

question: What vital piece of information should always be included in a patient referral letter?

options.A: The exact amount of money the patient has in savings
options.B: A detailed family history dating back three generations
options.C: The personal phone number of the village traditional ruler
options.D: Treatments and medications already given at the clinic

explanation: The receiving hospital must know what drugs or fluids have already been administered to prevent accidental overdosing. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h5)

question: Why is it necessary to stabilize an emergency patient before transporting them to a higher center?

options.A: To prove to the family that the clinic staff are intelligent
options.B: To make sure the ambulance driver gets paid on time
options.C: To prevent the patient's condition from worsening on the way
options.D: To reduce the paperwork needed at the receiving hospital

explanation: Basic stabilization, like securing an intravenous line or ensuring a patent airway, keeps the patient alive during travel. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h5)

question: How does a community health nurse help families who refuse a recommended hospital referral due to financial worries?

options.A: By telling them that hospitals in the city do not charge any money
options.B: By scolding them severely until they agree to borrow money from loan sharks
options.C: By counseling them on the risks of delay and exploring available support options
options.D: By hiding the referral letter so they do not worry about hospital bills

explanation: Nurses address fears and financial barriers through patient education, empathy, and connecting families with available community resources. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core responsibility of the community health nurse in a referral?

options.A: Writing a clear referral note detailing findings and treatments
options.B: Performing major complex surgeries at the primary clinic
options.C: Assessing the patient's condition to spot danger signs early
options.D: Conducting follow-up home visits after the patient returns

explanation: Primary health clinics do not have the facilities for major surgeries; such cases are referred upward. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which factor is a common logistical barrier to emergency referrals in rural communities?

options.A: An excessive surplus of functional ambulances
options.B: Poor road networks and lack of reliable transport
options.C: Too many specialists working in primary health posts
options.D: Free fuel supplies provided by local youth groups

explanation: Bad roads and lack of vehicles often delay the physical transfer of emergency patients to higher facilities. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: How can rude or harsh behavior by staff at a receiving hospital negatively affect the referral system?

options.A: It discourages patients and their relatives from seeking formal care in the future
options.B: It improves communication between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: It makes patients recover faster because they want to leave early
options.D: It encourages villagers to build more primary health care centers

explanation: Negative attitudes create a hostile environment, causing patients to avoid hospitals and patronize unqualified providers instead. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h7)

question: What is a counter-referral in community health practice?

options.A: Transferring a patient from a private clinic to a traditional healer
options.B: Reporting a nurse to the nursing council for writing a bad referral note
options.C: Sending a discharged patient back to their local clinic for follow-up care
options.D: Refusing to accept a patient into the teaching hospital due to lack of beds

explanation: A counter-referral brings the patient back to the primary level for continuous local monitoring after hospital treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)

question: A patient with hypertension is discharged from a federal teaching hospital. What should the local community health nurse do next?

options.A: Wait for the patient to develop a stroke before taking any action
options.B: Tell the patient never to visit the teaching hospital again for any reason
options.C: Monitor blood pressure regularly and check that prescribed drugs are taken correctly
options.D: Throw away the hospital discharge summary and start a new treatment plan

explanation: The nurse ensures continuity of care by supervising medication adherence and monitoring blood pressure at the local level. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)
